content:
Addition in Class 2 grows to 3-digit sums with carrying — a favourite in IMO and SOF Olympiad papers. Here is what the Maths Olympiad Class 2 addition chapter tests, the facts worth drilling, the usual mistakes, and a free 10-question test.

What the Class 2 Maths Olympiad Addition chapter tests

  • 2-digit and 3-digit addition, with and without carrying
  • Number bonds and mental addition strategies
  • Missing-number sentences like 40 + ▢ = 90
  • Word problems using "in all", "altogether" and "total"

Key facts your child should know

  • Add the ones first, then tens, then hundreds; carry when a column reaches 10 or more.
  • You may add in any order: 25 + 30 = 30 + 25.
  • Adding 0 changes nothing: 47 + 0 = 47.
  • Bonds to 100 (60 + 40) make mental maths fast.

Common mistakes to avoid

  • Forgetting to carry the ten (or hundred) when a column overflows.
  • Lining up the digits wrongly so tens add to ones.
  • Adding when the word problem actually asks how many are left.

faq.q: When do you carry in addition?
faq.a: Whenever a column adds to 10 or more — you write the ones digit and carry the extra ten into the next column.
Pairs of numbers that make a total, like 60 and 40 make 100. They speed up mental addition.
